message_1:
From: Alice Jiang <alice.jiang@acme-payments.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Cc: security@acme-payments.com
Date: Tue, 18 Nov 2025 13:12:00 +0000
Subject: New telemetry vendor (India) - quick confirmation on EU residency impact

Hi Naomi,

Quick one — our engineering team spotted that one of the telemetry vendors Redwood recently added (vendor ID: TelemetryWave) appears to process logs in an additional region (India). We have an upcoming audit where we need to confirm whether any EU-origin data for our account could be routed to or stored by that vendor.

Can you confirm:
- Whether TelemetryWave (or any new subcontractor added in the last 60 days) processes or stores EU-origin customer telemetry outside the EU;
- If yes, what contractual and technical controls are in place to prevent or limit cross-border transfers (onshore routing, pseudonymization, contractual safeguards);
- A snapshot (CSV is fine) of the minimal data types they receive when forwarding traces/logs to their backend.

We need a short answer and any supporting artefacts (DPA annex adjustments, onshore routing flags) by end of week if possible.

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Alice
Alice Jiang

Short answer up front: we do not route EU-origin customer PII outside of EU regions by default. However, certain telemetry partners are used for aggregated observability and may have processing nodes outside the EU unless an onshore routing flag is applied for a customer.

Action items we’ll take now:
- Pull a vendor snapshot for TelemetryWave (vendor onboarding doc + minimal data inventory) and share CSV by EOD tomorrow.
- Confirm any routing flags currently set on Acme’s account.
- Legal to confirm if DPA annex requires amendment for TelemetryWave and propose mitigations if necessary.

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Cc: Alice Jiang <alice.jiang@acme-payments.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Nov 2025 09:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: New telemetry vendor (India) - quick confirmation on EU residency impact

Folks — quick legal summary to support the call:

1) Contractual: TelemetryWave is on our subprocessor roster as of 2025-10-20. Our standard DPA includes a subprocessor clause with notice + objections; if the vendor processes outside the EU for accounts that require EU-only processing, we must either: (a) apply the onshore routing control to prevent routing to TelemetryWave, or (b) add an annex to the DPA listing TelemetryWave and confirm adequate safeguards (SCCs + encryption at rest).

2) Technical mitigations: If TelemetryWave only receives aggregated, pseudonymized metrics with no persistent identifiers we can document a compensating control; however the safer path for Acme (certified EU residency requirement) is to disable TelemetryWave for their account until we provide an attestation.

3) Next steps for the meeting:
- Rishi: bring a quick export showing account-level routing flags and a sample of the minimal telemetry CSV (redact identifiers),
- Naomi: bring the DPA excerpt and proposed annex language if needed,
- Marissa: confirm cutover window if we need to disable the integration.

I’ll prepare template annex language pre-call and attach to the follow‑up.

—Kimberly
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
